newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Howard not worried about Packer influence.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Howard not worried about Packer influence.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Friday he was not paranoid about the influence of publishing and television magnate Kerry Packer.

Howard, asked if he would be concerned if Packer acquired the bluechip newspaper group John Fairfax Holdings Ltd, said media policy would not be reviewed with a focus on the moguls who currently dominated the sector.

"I don't want to approach media policy in mogul-specific terms if I can put it that way," he said during an interview on the Australian Broadcasting Corp. "... but look I don't have a paranoia about Kerry Packer, no."
Howard said in another interview earlier on Friday that the cross-media rules governing the industry were an absurdity.

The rules prevent one person from controlling newspapers and electronic media in the same city, while foreign ownership restrictions prevent a single company from owning more than 15 percent with special permission.

"We will look at the cross media rules. I mean Packer, his whole family and his business has a very strong bacgkround (in the media sector). He is, as far as you might put (it), a wholly Australian-based operation."

Howard said the review of media policy was in effect a choice between retaining the status quo and therefore retaining the ownership instability, allowing a much higher level of foreign owernship, or having a much higher level of concentration in some area.
Rupert Murdoch, a U.S. citizen born in Australia, controls most of the metropolitan newspaper market through his News Corp Ltd publications.

Canadian publisher Conrad Black recently sold his 25 percent stake in Fairfax, frustrated at his inability to increase his stake under the foreign ownership rules and thereby thwart the ambitions which Packer and, until recently, Murdoch, had on Fairfax.
Black sold his stake to Brierley Investments Ltd.
